properties.decision:
Recorded as brainstorming, not as a proposal. Anthony, 2026-09-14, in his words: "one of my projects (flo2) with my brother Alex. We'll use the same projects repo (same GitHub repo). When I am looking at the project, it should be viewed from my lens/persona. When he is looking at the project, it should be viewed from his lens. When opening an existing project, I usually run where-am-i skill. Maybe this would be a good place to see who the current user is? Probably if it is coming from the same machine, it is probably the same user, so may not need to ask every time and do something like 'assuming you are AJ; if not, please state your name and some background so that I can shape/tailor my responses to you'."

WHAT IS ALREADY ON THE RECORD, so this is the new part and not a restatement: the guess-from-login idea is his own from 2026-08-18 (dec:idea-a-user-carries-a-persona-that-shapes-every-reply) and is already law in the accepted requirement — "a login name, a git author or an existing handle is a reasonable offer and a terrible silent default" (req:the-agent-learns-who-it-is-talking-to, accepted on his word today). The orientation skill already says "ask once, at the start, if the design does not already say", and the lens on every reply already lists the recorded backgrounds and says "this says what the DESIGN holds, never who is at the keyboard".

THE NEW CASE, which none of that settles: a design that records TWO backgrounds. "Ask if the design does not already say" is ambiguous when the design says two things. Which one applies is a fact about the SESSION, not about the design — a seat names a session, never a person, and the graph cannot hold "who is reading right now" without asserting what it cannot know. So the choice is made per session, every session, and today nothing says how or where.

WHAT THE AGENT CAN SEE THAT THE GRAPH CANNOT (measured on this box): git user.name "Anthony Sligar", git user.email, OS login "ajs7". The recorded Contributors carry handles "@ajs" and "@bro" — nothing joins a git identity to a Contributor, so today a match is a guess by name, not a lookup.

OPTIONS, unranked:
(a) SKILL-ONLY: the orientation step gains a clause for the several-backgrounds case — offer the one whose name matches the git author or login as an assumption ("assuming you are AJ — if not, say who you are and your background"), invite correction, and do not ask afresh. Cheap; instruction-only; nothing observes whether it happens, and the design has measured that instruction-only rules lapse within days.
(b) MAKE THE MATCH A LOOKUP: record the identity signal a harness can see (a git author name or handle) on the Contributor, and let the lens line carry it — "Recorded backgrounds: who:ajs (git: Anthony Sligar), who:alex (git: Alex …)" — so the agent's guess is a join, not a hunch. Counter: identity signals in a PUBLIC export — the 2026-08-19 redaction precedent; a name is probably fine, an email is not, and the design should say which.
(c) THE SEAT CARRIES THE READER: once offered and confirmed (or offered and unanswered), the session's seat records "reader: who:ajs, basis: assumed from git author / confirmed by them", and every lens line says so — "speaking to who:ajs (assumed, unconfirmed)". The assumption becomes visible and correctable on every reply instead of silent, and it expires with the session, which is exactly the lifetime a "who is reading" fact has. Answers dec:idea-the-persona-has-no-delivery-leg-so-what-carries-it's question for this case. Counter: seat state grows; an assumption repeated on every reply can become wallpaper.
(d) NEVER GUESS; ask each session when more than one background is recorded. Counter: it is exactly what he asked not to have, and a question every session teaches people to answer it carelessly.

THE HONEST COUNTER TO THE PREMISE: same machine is not same person. Alex at Anthony's desk, a shared laptop, a hosted flo2 where every session comes from one server — in each the machine signal points at the wrong person, and the accepted requirement's "offered, never assumed" is what keeps a wrong guess cheap. (c) is the option that keeps the wrong guess visible for the whole session rather than for one sentence.

A SECOND COUNTER: the persona is per-graph (established 2026-08-19). For flo2, one repo means one graph, so both brothers ARE in it — this case works. Across their other projects each answers again; that is unchanged by anything here.
properties.name: OPEN — when two people share one design (flo2: Anthony and Alex, one repo), the graph records BOTH backgrounds and cannot say which one is reading; should orientation offer a guess from the machine ("assuming you are AJ — if not, say who you are and your background") rather than ask every session, and where does the confirmed answer live?
properties.rationale: Recorded as its own question rather than folded into the persona idea because the persona idea asks WHETHER a stored background is the right mechanism and the accepted requirement says WHAT is owed; this asks the operational question neither settles — which of several recorded readers a session is talking to, how the agent guesses, and where a confirmed guess lives for the rest of the session. The cheap option (a) is his stated ask; (c) is the one that keeps a wrong guess visible, which is what the accepted requirement's "offered, never assumed" is really for.
